title: Large shrine cedar with stringy moss-streaked bark under an overcast sky
status: PHOTO-DERIVED REPRESENTATIVES. Textures are synthesised from regions of one photograph; the photograph was not taken at Aokigahara unless stated.

source.colour_handling: embedded profile "Display P3" converted to sRGB with LittleCMS (relative colorimetric)
source.rights_note: Supplied by the repository owner as a personal photograph of a shrine tree. The sacred rope and paper streamers are excluded from every region. Not captured at Aokigahara.

sun_estimate.basis: overcast sky, no shadows; the elevation is not observable and does not enter the preset

analysis: analysis over the whole frame minus exclude_rects

notes: The sun azimuth relative to the camera is unknown; it was fitted on a 30 degree grid.
fit_exposure absorbs the camera exposure and is not the preset exposure.
The dome image is rendered with the viewer sun azimuth (155 deg) and the pack sun elevation.

preset.label: Large shrine cedar with stringy moss-streaked bark under an overcast sky (photo-derived)

measurements.split_method: Otsu on log illumination (blur sigma 70 px); Otsu split was one-sided, used the upper/lower 30 % of the blurred luminance
measurements.sun_elevation_basis: overcast sky, no shadows; the elevation is not observable and does not enter the preset

derivation.lit_shade_split: lit and shaded pixels are separated by large-scale illumination (blurred luminance), so texture contrast such as bright rootlets over dark crevices does not count as sunlight
derivation.sun_and_hemi: hemi = clip(1.9 - 0.3*log2(1 + direct/ambient), 0.9, 1.9); sun = clip(ratio*hemi*0.9, 0.4, 3.6). Calibrated so the three existing presets (overcast 0.55/1.9, soft 2.0/1.35, clear 3.3/0.9) are reproduced from their implied ratios.
derivation.hemiSky: visible sky mean, luma matched to the existing presets
derivation.hemiGround: ground probe mean, luma matched to the existing presets (0.19)
derivation.fog: far-background probe mean, luma matched to the existing presets (0.58)
derivation.turb_ray_mie: fitted to the visible sky with the viewer Sky shader
derivation.exposure: clip(0.9 + (median luma - 0.35)*0.6, 0.85, 1.05): brighter photographs get a slightly higher exposure
derivation.sun_colour: the viewer keeps sun.color fixed (setHSL(.09,.28,.9)); the measured direct-light tint is reported for reference only

lighting.usage: Add the preset object to PRESETS in viewer/app.js (see preset_snippet.js). Values are calibrated to the existing presets, not absolute radiometry.

grade.derivation: black/white from the 0.5/99.5 luma percentiles (limited to 0.12/0.85), gamma so that input 0.42 maps to the photo median, split-toning with the measured shadow/highlight tints, saturation relative to 0.40 mean HSV saturation
grade.usage: three.js LUTCubeLoader + LUTPass on the tone-mapped frame, or any .cube-aware grading tool

materials.notes: Lower trunk below the rope: long stringy fibrous bark with a green moss band and a strip of exposed pinkish inner bark; buttress flare at the bottom. Both silhouettes visible; unwrapped as a cylinder.

synthesis.method: Efros-Freeman image quilting on a torus (seamless in x and y); candidates drawn from the source and its horizontal mirror

physical_scale.note: region width is an estimate; the tile scale follows from it. Detail above source_texels_per_metre is interpolation, not observation.

synthetic_micro_grain.reason: the source was enlarged before synthesis; a 3 % periodic grain masks interpolation blur and is not observed detail

maps.diff: sRGB albedo, illumination flattened (large-scale shading and colour drift divided out); the photograph's illuminant is NOT neutralised
maps.nor_gl: OpenGL tangent-space normal derived from the luminance height proxy (not a scanned surface)
maps.rough: heuristic: 0.88 base for class 'bark', modulated by fine luminance
maps.height: luminance band mix (fine/mid/coarse), percentile-normalised; dark = low. Ambient occlusion, if wanted, is 1 - k*max(0, blur(height) - height) at two radii

sky_equirect.mapping: three.js EquirectangularReflectionMapping (u = atan2(z, x)/2pi + 0.5, v = asin(y)/pi + 0.5, top row = zenith)
sky_equirect.content: upper hemisphere: Sky.js port with fitted parameters through ACES filmic and sRGB; lower hemisphere: ground probe colour, darkened downward

not_claimed: No map is a scanned or photogrammetric surface: normal, roughness, height and AO are heuristics from image luminance.
Albedo keeps the photograph's illuminant and white balance; only large-scale shading was flattened.
Sky parameters are a fit to a handful of sky pixels with an unknown sun azimuth; sun elevation is a visual estimate.
Lighting preset numbers are calibrated to the viewer's existing presets, not to measured radiometry.
Physical scales rest on an estimated region width.
Species, site and season are not established by any of this.
